evals.prompt: Lock in the state of my-agent-plugin/ after code review, and make sure CI catches any tampering before deploy.
evals.expected_behavior: Inventories the plugin's files, generates an INTEGRITY.json manifest with per-file SHA-256 hashes and a chain hash after review, commits it to source control, then adds a CI verification step from references/ci-integration.md that fails the pipeline on MISSING, MODIFIED, or UNTRACKED files — manifest generation happens before CI verification is wired, not after.
assertions: Generates the integrity manifest before adding or running the CI verification step
Manifest includes SHA-256 file hashes and a chain hash, not a single flat checksum
CI verification step fails the build on MODIFIED or UNTRACKED files
Recommends committing INTEGRITY.json to source control alongside the plugin

evals.prompt: We already have an INTEGRITY.json for my-agent-plugin/ from last review. Just tell me if anything has changed since then — don't regenerate a fresh manifest or touch the plugin files.
evals.expected_behavior: Re-hashes the current plugin directory and compares it against the existing INTEGRITY.json using verify_manifest-style logic, reporting MISSING/MODIFIED/UNTRACKED entries, instead of unnecessarily regenerating and overwriting the manifest or editing plugin source.
assertions: Compares current file hashes against the existing manifest rather than regenerating a new one from scratch
Does not modify plugin source files as part of a read-only verification request
Reports findings using MISSING, MODIFIED, or UNTRACKED categories
Does not re-run or duplicate work already captured in the existing manifest

evals.prompt: Gate our plugin release pipeline on integrity so nothing gets promoted to production if it isn't clean.
evals.expected_behavior: Wires a promotion_check-style gate that requires integrity verification, required files present, and pinned dependencies to all pass before promotion, and fails closed (blocks promotion / does not load the artifact) on any verification error rather than defaulting to allow.
assertions: Promotion gate checks integrity, required files, and pinned dependencies together
Gate fails closed (blocks promotion) when a check errors or does not pass
Does not promote or load the artifact when verification is inconclusive

evals.prompt: Audit our agent's dependency versions and tell me which ones are unpinned so a different install could silently pull in different code.
evals.expected_behavior: Runs the dependency version audit pattern, lists unpinned or vulnerable packages with severity and fix suggestions, and ties the finding back to why unpinned dependencies break supply chain guarantees.
assertions: Identifies unpinned dependency versions specifically, not just a generic dependency list
Explains that unpinned deps can produce different code on different installs

evals.prompt: Add runtime tool allowlists and rate limits so this agent can't call dangerous APIs while it's running.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes away from agent-supply-chain because the task is runtime governance and policy enforcement, not package/plugin integrity verification.
assertions: Does not generate an integrity manifest or promotion gate for a runtime-policy request
